name: raw_schema
query: SELECT column_name,datatype,unit,ucd,description FROM TAP_SCHEMA.columns WHERE table_name='dbo.raw'

rows.description: Estimated size of the downloaded file in KBytes. It is only "estimated" as in general, FITS headers can be patched at download time, making the file size varying with time.)
A URL that can be used to download the raw file; if the file is under proprietary period, only authenticated users with the necessary access rights will be given access to it.

A URL that can be used to find the access points of the raw file itself, and of all its related files. Related files are: the calibration files necessary to reduce a science raw frame (see calSelector entries), and, if available, a (list of) calibrated product(s) generated out of it.)
The content of the DATE_OBS keyword exposed as a string and not a datetime field (ESO_DATEADD_SEC does not work on this column, use exp_start instead).
Declination FK5 J2000
Pointing Declination FK5 J2000 of the telescope
Detector chip identification. Read from keyword DET CHIP1 ID (alias DET CHIP ID). Example: HASCI03
Number of cycles for chopping. Read from keyword DET CHOP NCYCLES. Example:  1
Detector Integration Time (Infrared instruments).
Unique exposure ID number. Read from keyword DET EXP ID (aliases DET EXPO NO, DET EXP NO).
Number of exposures, each with det_dit integration time (Infrared instruments).
Observation category: SCIENCE,CALIB,ACQUISITION,TECHNICAL,TEST,SIMULATION,OTHER
The main unique ESO archive file identifier
Mode/technique used for the observation
Type of observation/exposure
Ecliptic latitude of the observation.
Ecliptic longitude of the observation.
The start time of the observation (format: ISO-8601).
Total exposure time on target.
All filters.  The string is in the format <value>,<value>,... where <value> is the value of one of the keywords INS.FILT*.NAME
Galactic latitude of the observation.
Galactic longitude of the observation.
All gratings. The string is in the format <value>, <value>,... where <value> is the value of one of the keywords INS.GRAT*.NAME.
All grisms.  The string is in the format <value>, <value>,...  where <value> is the value of one of the keywords INS.GRIS*.NAME. Example: GRIS_600B
Instrument mode
Instrument name
[nm] Maximum wavelength of the overall transmission curve (filter + detector + optics); currently available only for images.
[nm] Minimum wavelength of the overall transmission curve (filter + detector + optics); currently available only for images.
The last modification date of this record (format: ISO-8601).
Modified Julian Date (JD - 2400000.5) of the start of the observation.
The identifier of the ESO Observation Block, a unique numeric ID assigned by the Observation Handling System
The name of the ESO Observation Block
Target designation as given by the astronomer, though at times overwritten by the obeservatory, especially for CALIB observations. Compare with the similar field called "target".)
Service or Visitor mode
The original file name as used on the instrument workstation at the telescope. Read from keyword ORIGFILE. Example: HD75289_0012.fits
ESO proposal cycle
Names of the Principal and Co-Investigators
ESO program run identification code
Title of the observing programme
Program type: 0=Normal, 1=GTO, 2=DDT, 3=ToO, 4=Large, 5=Short, 6=Calibration, 7=Monitoring MAPPING
Right Ascension FK5 J2000
Pointing Right Ascension FK5 J2000 of the telescope
The date at which the data become publicly available at the end of the proprietary period

This is the field to be used for spatial queries. Example: select * from dbo.raw where contains( s_region, circle('', 56.3, 20, 1)=1  to search in a cone of 1 deg radius around ra=56.3 dec=20. In output it provides the spatial coordinates of the raw data set expressed as POSITION ra dec, as, for raw data, the footprints of the observations are currently not available.
All slits. The string is in the format <value>, <value>,... where <value> is the value of one of the keywords INS.SLIT*.NAME.
Target designation (as given by the astronomer)
The airmass at the end of the observation.
The airmass at the start of the observation.
The Altitude angle (deg) at the start of the observation.
Site seeing at the end of the observation as measured by the ASM (Astronomical Site Monitor). FWHM at 0.5 um, in arcseconds.
Site seeing at the start of the observation as measured by the ASM (Astronomical Site Monitor). FWHM at 0.5 um, in arcseconds.
Average site barometric air pressure at the end of the observation, as measured by the ASM (Astronomical Site Monitor). Expressed in hectopascal.
Average site barometric air pressure at the start of the observation, as measured by the ASM (Astronomical Site Monitor). Expressed in hectopascal.
Average ambient relative humidity at the observation site, as measured by the ASM (Astronomical Site Monitor). Expressed as a percentage.
The Azimuth angle (deg) S=0,W=90 at the start of the observation.
The name of the telescope.
The exposure number within its template execution.
The observing template identifier, a unique ID assigned to a template, that is, to a pre-defined sequence of operations involving any combination of telescope, instrument and detector actions
The name of the observing template.
The total number of exposures for the given template.
The template sequence number within the Observing Block
The start time of the execution of the observing template, exposed as a string and not as a datetime field as this is used as an identifier (ESO_DATEADD_SEC does not work on this column).
